lesson_title: The Six Machines Hiding in Your Bicycle
hook_text: Your bicycle is not one machine. It is at least five simple machines pretending to be one.
clip_script: Every machine ever built is made from six simple ones. Lever: a bar on a pivot. Wheel and axle: a doorknob. Pulley: a grooved wheel with a rope. Ramp. Wedge: an axe. Screw: a ramp wrapped round a rod. Now look at a bicycle. Pedals and crank: wheel and axle. Chain and sprockets: gears, which are wheels with teeth. Brake handles: levers. Saddle clamp: a screw. Each one gives a mechanical advantage, which is just the load divided by your push. Bigger than 1, the machine made you stronger. Smaller than 1, it made you faster. And the price is always distance: a long ramp for a small push. That is the whole of mechanical systems in one bicycle.
visual_style: Whiteboard bicycle outline; each part lights up in turn and a label names the simple machine; a ramp and a drum appear at the end with a long arrow and a small arrow.
pacing: Six quick definitions, then five parts of the bicycle, then the one-line rule about distance.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find three simple machines in your kitchen.
